newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez seen posting 725 mln Ffr profit.
newsitem.headline: Suez seen posting 725 mln Ffr profit.

text.p: French holding Compagnie de Suez is expected to announce on Wednesday a first-half 1996 net attributable profit of about 725 million francs, an average of analysts' predictions showed.

Forecasts for the company's profits range from 500 million to 900 million francs, any of which would compare favourably with the company's first-half 1995 loss of 3.96 billion francs, which included a 4.076 billion franc charge for real estate provisions.
Analysts said the results were unlikely to entail surprises and that they were more interested in getting a clear statement of medium term strategy from the group's chairman Gerard Mestrallet.

They said results should be boosted by strong performance of the group's units and by capital gains from asset sales, but cautioned that Suez might still suffer from its exposure to France's troubled real estate sector.

One analyst predicted a 500 million franc real estate charge in the first half, while another said Suez would have to take about a one billion franc charge for the year as he estimated real estate would eat up about 850 million francs of Suez's cash flow in 1996.
Other analysts said they would not be surprised if the company announced an acceleration in the sale of real estate assets which would raise the level of capital losses in the results.

The strong performance of financial markets in the first six months of the year will make the bank's contribution to Suez's consolidated net results positive. In the first six months of 1995, the bank contributed a 16 million franc loss to Suez results.
Suez results should also be helped by good results at Societe General de Belgique, Sofinco and Factofrance Heller, analysts said.
The company's results are expected to be boosted by a 1.3 billion franc capital gain from the sale of Suez's 75 percent stake in Gartmore GMR.L to Natwest.
Banque Indosuez will be included in the company's accounts for the last time. The sale of 53.17 percent of its capital to Caisse Nationale des Credit Agricole did not occur until July 1 of this year.
